jOOQ on The ORM Foundation? I am the one who maintains jOOQ and I would like to bring my unit framework back to the standard (in case you want to seriously consider doing so). It's about time honestly. In short, what I did was to replace all logic and implementation in the OO classes with java.lang.Object injectable instances. I removed the original logic in OO classes. Only default implementations of OO methods are provided and all others, those that exist in the framework's OO classes, are declared private and only invoked using OO. Default implementations are kept synchronized. Now, if you call any OO method from OO, i.e., from DAO or from any Expression, you get the java.lang.Object being in control. Even if you invoke the AA method from the JOOXUnit class inside the same OO class, the method is invoked through the java.lang.Object, meaning that the OO class is an Expression and not an Object. This, I believe, fixes the internal bugs present because of the presence of OO and eliminates the possibility of running into bugs due to the very nature of JOOQ. I would like to hear your opinion. A lot has been said already in this thread and I expect we will continue to have discussions about this for a while. But it is worth noting that if you look at the RDBMS stack in general we have a lot of similar (interdependent) technology.

Essentially the RDBMS is about data (either metadata or data itself). We have tried to get between data and other objects like models, controllers and entity objects. As such ORM was really a mechanism to get between the RDBMS and the “models” (such as objects for a controller).
